title: Conditional tests leave a shared decay error uncertain in 17 active USGS aftershock forecast regions
abstract: We tested the time and magnitude shapes of first USGS Reasenberg-Jones forecasts using a published ComCat snapshot from November 2026. Conditional event times remove any scalar productivity and its uncertainty. We reconstructed the first-week counts exactly for 235 forecasts. At conservative magnitude cuts, only 17 regions had events on days 1 to 7 (75 earthquakes, 16 overlap clusters). With each earthquake given equal weight, the fitted change in decay exponent was -0.77 (95% cluster bootstrap limits -1.16 to -0.23). With each active sequence given equal weight, it was -0.57 (-1.42 to 0.17). The full-week change was near zero. Higher magnitude cuts left too few events to resolve the error. The large-event share was consistent with the stated b value. An exploratory background check did not remove the late-time signal, but had uncertain rates. Thus the evidence suggests a late tail in the pooled events but does not establish a shared decay error across sequences. A productivity correction alone cannot alter these conditional shapes. The package gives code, sufficient statistics, input hashes, numerical checks and a fixed-snapshot reproduction script. This is a new shape test on earlier data, not an independent replication or proof of physical cause.

display.caption: Conditional event times and fitted decay changes. Zero is the issued decay exponent. Each active sequence has equal weight in the right panel; bars show 95% overlap-cluster bootstrap limits. The primary interval includes zero.
